key_insight: The paper proves that Gradient Equilibrium (GEQ) and Blackwell approachability are algorithmically equivalent, linking GEQ to regret minimization and calibration through known online learning equivalences.
engineering_relevance: This lets practitioners transfer mature online-learning guarantees and algorithms—such as optimism and strong adaptivity—directly to GEQ-based systems like online conformal prediction.
method: Constructs efficient reductions from Blackwell approachability to a black-box GEQ oracle and back.
Shows the reductions preserve asymptotic error rates, establishing equivalence in an algorithmic sense.
Derives necessary and sufficient conditions for GEQ and connects constrained vs. unconstrained decision-set variants.
evidence_signal: The main evidence is theoretical: the abstract reports formal reductions and equivalence results rather than empirical evaluation or benchmark data.
watch_item: The guarantees are asymptotic and reduction-based, so practical performance depends on the quality, stability, and computational cost of the underlying oracle implementations.
paper_title: Blackwell Approachability and Gradient Equilibrium are Equivalent
